Sports.title: Amy Hunt clinches European Championships sprint double: Team GB golden girl beats rival Dina Asher-Smith in 200m final
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Amy Hunt completed a brilliant sprint double by landing 200m gold in Birmingham – but warned there will be no celebrating until her target of four is complete.

The 24-year-old is seeking a historic quadruple this week and is now halfway there after blitzing the field in 22.19.

Dina Asher-Smith was the last sprinter to double up at this competition eight years ago but could only manage bronze on this occasion.

The home hopefuls were in adjacent lanes and Asher-Smith got the better start around the bend as she sought a seventh European gold.

But Hunt reeled her compatriot in on the home straight as the domestic duel lived up to expectations in front of an improved crowd of more than 20,000 at the Alexander Stadium.

'The 100 is the hardest mentally and the 200 is the hardest physically,' Hunt told the BBC.

Amy Hunt completed the sprint double by adding 200m gold to her triumph in the 100m

Hunt clinched victory ahead of her rival Dina Asher-Smith, who claimed the bronze medal

'I've had a lot of health things going on this year, some really low blood pressure, and the 200s have been really scary. I have been fainting after some of my 200s this year.

'I just had to go into that one, get on the bend and be really brave. It was an amazing race.'

Asher-Smith has now won nine European medals, putting her one shy of the all-time record, but this was the latest sign of a changing of the guard.

Hunt retained her national 100m title by beating Asher-Smith on this track in June before dethroning her over the same distance on the opening night of these Championships.

Asher-Smith still leads the 200m head-to-head between the two but Hunt has come of age in the last 12 months and now set her sights on completing a remarkable quadruple as she looks ahead to the women's and mixed 4x100m relays over the weekend.

'This is becoming a magical week and one I will remember for the rest of my life,' she said.

'There is no celebrating or champagne until Sunday night. I have a debt to the ladies, we have to come out here and show them who the best sprint nation is in Europe. It's not over yet – I hope you're not sick of my face.'

Asher-Smith said: 'Obviously, I'm disappointed to have a bronze, but I think 10 years after my first one it is such an achievement to be in a place to come back year after year.

Hunt signalled that she had won two of her targeted four golds, with her focus now turning to the relays

'It doesn't matter what's going on in my life, I just want to continue to be one of the fastest women in the world. I'm happy to have done that and it is great to be part of a successful British team.'

The hosts' pair finished either side of Ireland's Rhasidat Adeleke, who won silver in a 22.28 national record.

Keely Hodgkinson kept her bid for a European hat-trick on track on a dramatic afternoon which saw her main rival Audrey Werro take a tumble – before being reinstated for the final.

Hodgkinson won the second semi-final in 1:57.38, holding off Femke Broeders-Bol to safely advance to one of the most eagerly-awaited events of the week tonight.

It was a far more serene race than the opening semi, which was dominated by Werro before she hit the deck on the final bend.

Werro picked herself up to stumble over the finish line and a successful appeal means the 22-year-old, who holds this year's world lead, will also be on the start line.

Hodgkinson was relieved to avoid the chaos and said: 'You can't worry about what happened to other people, but I hope she's ok.

'The excitement makes me excited. I love a good challenge and I hope for a clean race with no falling over and no wind.'

Scot Jemma Reekie took advantage of Werro's slip to cross the line first and advance in 1:58.61.

Novuna is the Official Finance Partner of British Athletics and proud sponsor of the GB & NI Athletics Team.

Sports.title: Rangers suffer latest European humiliation after  crashing out of Europa League qualifying with embarrassing defeat by Polish minnows: Pressure already growing on Derek McInnes
Sports.content:
In the build-up to this Europa League qualifier against Jagiellonia Bialystok, Rangers manager Derek McInnes had spoken of how the club were ‘playing with fire’.

His words were in reference to the lack of bodies in key positions. Down to the bare bones at left-back, it was a hurry-up aimed at the club’s board and recruitment department.

Yet, on a night when McInnes was chasing his first win as manager, the unfancied Poles turned up at Ibrox, doused the place in petrol and lit a match.

Make no mistake, McInnes is in serious danger of being engulfed by the flames even this early in his tenure. The vitriolic reaction from fans at full-time made that abundantly clear.

His team are nothing short of a shambles. He can moan about a lack of cover in certain positions all he wants. The reality is that he is not getting the best out of those players under his command.

The blame for this Europa League exit lies squarely at his door. No one else’s.

Cammy Devlin, Findlay Curtis and Lawrence Shankland react to a bitterly disappointing result

Rangers will now drop down into the Europa Conference League qualifiers, where they will face Jablonec of Czechia.

Given the way the atmosphere turned toxic towards the end, this had echoes of Russell Martin against Club Brugge last season.

At least Martin had the excuse that Brugge were actually a very decent Champions League side. Jagiellonia are second-rate opposition – and Rangers still couldn’t beat them.

At the end, many of the Rangers players slumped to their knees, before awkwardly circling around the pitch to applaud the supporters.

There was no gratitude to be found from those who stayed. Instead, torrents of abuse and boos rained down from a fanbase already at their wits end even this early in the campaign.

A long, long season lies in store on the evidence Rangers have produced over their first four matches, none of which have yielded a win.

Nico Raskin was posted missing again last night and was hooked shortly after the Poles had equalised midway through the second half.

Other players such as Manny Fernandez and Ryan Naderi are miles – absolutely miles – off the required standard to succeed at a club like Rangers.

Nik Prelec heads home the goal that silenced Ibrox and ended Rangers' Europa League hopes

It may still be early in the season but this was a horribly damaging night for McInnes on the back of the home defeat to Hibs last weekend.

The injury to Tuur Rommens, along with the absence of any other competent left-sided defender, forced McInnes into another reshuffle and change of system. He opted for a back three of Fernandez, Dujon Sterling and Olwethu Makhanya, with Djeidi Gassama and Daisuke Yokota deployed as the wing-backs.

The chopping and changing between systems and personnel has been a prominent feature of these early weeks of the McInnes era, albeit this one was forced upon him.

After only coming off the bench for the final five minutes of last week’s first leg in Poland, Lawrence Shankland was restored to the starting XI.

This felt like a big night for the newly appointed captain, both in terms of proving he can cut it at a higher level than the SPFL Premiership and also his ability to lead by example.

Jagiellonia were having a fair amount of joy down the flanks in the early stages. Particularly down their right flank, with Gassama guilty of switching off far too often.

Rangers were fortunate not to fall behind on 14 minutes when a slick move from the Poles cut the home side wide open straight through the middle.

Jesus Imaz latched on to a neat through ball and only had Ivor Pandur to beat, but his shot came back off the post and the ball was eventually scrambled clear.

Rangers players were left to contemplate a season in the Conference League... at best

That was the cue for a section of the Ibrox crowd to erupt in anger, clearly less than enamoured at what they were watching and with Europa League qualification in serious danger of slipping away.

There was no question the stadium was growing tense and nervy even so early in the contest. It was a timely boost, then, when Rangers took the lead on 18 minutes.

Operating from the right wing, Yokota was comfortably Rangers’ brightest player in attack and he was instrumental in the move which eventually led to the award of a penalty.

A handball against former Celtic defender Yuki Kobayashi was spotted by the VAR and the referee was called over to the monitor. Shankland stepped up and calmly clipped the ball straight down the middle as Ibrox breathed a much-needed sigh of relief.

Dan Neil was having a decent game in midfield, with his energy and ability to read the play leading to Rangers winning the ball high up the pitch on a number of occasions.

Neil has been one of nine new summer signings thus far. For all that McInnes may bemoan the lack of options in certain positions, the reality is that he has still been well backed by the board.

With the tie now poised at 2-2 on aggregate, Rangers still had plenty of work to do and Thelo Aasgaard flashed a low shot just wide of the target on 35 minutes as they chased a second goal.

However, at the back, Rangers still looked far from convincing. There was a huge let-off seven minutes before half-time when Jagiellonia forward Nik Prelec skewed a shot wide after a good cross from Rodrigo Conceicao.

Even though his side had the lead on the night, McInnes clearly was not overly impressed with what he had seen in the opening 45 minutes. Aasgaard was hooked at half-time and Ross McCrorie was brought on at left-back as the manager reverted to a back four.

Decked out in their red-and-yellow kit, and backed by a decent travelling support, Jagiellonia sensed this was there for them.

Daichi Yokota was Rangers' most creative player but in truth they were very poor on the night

It had been noted by a pundit on radio that ‘they kind of look like Partick Thistle a little bit’, in reference to the colour of jerseys worn by the Poles. Sadly for Rangers, the same reference could be made about them in terms of their performance levels. Plainly, this was a very tough watch.

Dull, nervy and laboured throughout, it was no surprise when Rangers finally caved and conceded an equaliser on 65 minutes.

Jagiellonia switched the play a couple of times to stretch the home defence, before Andrea Klynge swung over a good cross to the back post. Having fluffed his lines in the first half, Prelec made no mistake on this occasion as he bulleted a header past Pandur and into the net.

With the Poles now leading 3-2 on aggregate, this was utterly desperate from Rangers. No substance, no backbone, no leadership, no quality, no style of play – and absolutely no idea about what they were being asked to do.

On as a substitute, Bojan Miovski glanced a header just wide of the target with only a couple of minutes left to play.

The truth is that Rangers didn’t deserve to go through. They have regressed from last season. A League Cup tie with St Mirren on Sunday is a match McInnes dare not lose.

Sports.title: Former Chelsea doctor Eva Carneiro takes aim at Jose Mourinho and John Terry as she reignites row over infamous touchline spat after ex-manager refused to apologise in new documentary
Sports.content:
Former Chelsea doctor Eva Carneiro takes aim at Jose Mourinho and John Terry as she reignites row over infamous touchline spat after ex-manager refused to apologise in new documentary

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Chelsea's former doctor Eva Carneiro has taken aim at Jose Mourinho after he stood by his alleged verbal abuse of her in his new documentary.

Mourinho has refused to apologise to Carneiro for their infamous touchline row which saw him allegedly brand her a 'daughter of a whore' in Portuguese.

In his Netflix docu-series 'MOURINHO', he justifies his behaviour in the flashpoint which occurred against Swansea City in 2015 when Carneiro and physio Jon Fearn ran on the pitch to treat Eden Hazard, who had seemingly gone down injured.

Now Carneiro has said on X: '11 years on and here we are reliving the worst. Hope they made some money.'

She also hit out at John Terry, who stood by Mourinho in the documentary, saying: 'We are bound by a medico-legal code of conduct. Genuinely it would be healthy for John Terry to learn the rules of the game. It’s been long enough mate.'

In a separate post, she added: 'So it is really simple. Referee Michael Oliver called us on TWICE, player Eden Hazard requested medical assistance, we then made eye contact from side line and he confirmed he needed medical assistance, TWICE. At that point my hands are bound as a medical professional.'

Chelsea's former doctor Eva Carneiro has had a dig at Jose Mourinho after he refused to apologise for their spat in his new documentary

Carneiro and Mourinho clashed in 2015 when she went on the pitch to treat Eden Hazard

Mourinho hit the roof when Carneiro and physio Jon Fearn went onto the pitch to treat Eden Hazard, who had gone down seemingly injured.

He called her 'impulsive and naive' in his first public reaction to her decision to treat Hazard. She was then dropped from first-team duties and left the club just a month later.

Mourinho and Chelsea eventually agreed a settlement after Carneiro took them to a tribunal over claims that she was discriminated against by the manager, and constructively dismissed by the club.

Eleven years on, Mourinho believes he treated Carneiro in the same manner that he would treat a male doctor.

‘For me, a lady doctor is the same as a man’s doctor,' Mourinho said in the docu-series. 'So, as always, I use my vocabulary when I’m not happy.

'There are words in moments where the tension is very, very high. Normally, people with football culture, with football DNA, with football background, they go over it in one second. In that case, it was different.’

Hazard, who played under the now-63-year-old for two years, claimed 'it was nothing special' in the documentary, which is set to air on Tuesday, but 'with Jose everything is bigger'.

Footage shows that the Portuguese coach, who is now Real Madrid manager, shouted a whole host of expletives toward Carneiro and Fearn as they treated Hazard. He screamed phrases such as 'f*** off, man' and 'f*** you, man'.

Mourinho has spoken up about the incident for the first time in over a decade in Netflix's new three-part docu-series MOURINHO

'I’m not a doctor, but my eyes know when a player is injured, and they know when a player is not injured,' Mourinho said in the docu-series.

'I knew that he was not injured, but the doctors went to the pitch, and in that moment we were left with nine players.’

Hazard was forced to come off the pitch for a brief period, as is the rule when a player receives medical treatment, leaving Chelsea with nine men after Thibaut Courtois had been sent off.

Terry, who was Chelsea's captain during both of Mourinho's stints at Stamford Bridge, claimed it was well known by both players and staff that the manager did not want team doctor's to attend to players unless the injuries looked serious.

Speaking in MOURINHO, he said: ‘Medically, he would say unless it’s really, really bad, then they’re [the team doctors] not coming on. That was the understanding for us as players; the medical staff, everyone bought into that.

‘It was a big moment obviously and he took a lot of backlash for that. There was a lot of heat on the football club.’

Chelsea gave Dr Carneiro an unreserved apology, but Mourinho refused to say sorry and grinned as he left the tribunal.

A deal was done in a back corridor of the court and Chelsea then issued a statement saying it 'regretted the circumstances' which led to the former club doctor leaving and 'apologises unreservedly to her and her family for the distress caused'.

The terms of the settlement remain secret, but during the tribunal it was revealed that Chelsea had previously offered £1.2million to silence Carneiro.

Mourinho did not apologise after the incident or at the tribunal and there were no signs of an apology in the docu-series either.

The three-part documentary combs through the career of Mourinho, covering the various highs and lows from his three decades in the professional game, from his winning mentality and undeniable ability to secure silverware to his many, many controversies.

Terry and Frank Lampard are just two of a host of Mourinho's former players who provide anecdotes and insight into the manager, who has won 26 major trophies during his career on the touchline.

Sports.title: Puerto Rican boxer Prichard Colon dies over a decade on from suffering catastrophic injuries during fight that left him in a coma
Sports.content:
Puerto Rican boxer Prichard Colon dies over a decade on from suffering catastrophic injuries during fight that left him in a coma

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former boxer Prichard Colon has died at the age of 33 more than a decade after suffering catastrophic brain injuries.

Back in October 2015 Colon, competing as a super-middleweight at the time, suffered a bleed on the brain after taking repeated blows to the back of the head during a contest with America's Terrel Williams in Virginia.

After vomiting and collapsing in the dressing room after his defeat, the Puerto Rican was rushed to hospital before spending 221 days in a coma. The fight with Williams had seen part of his skull collapse as a result of the repeated rabbit punches, which are deemed illegal in the sport.

After emerging from the coma, Colon, once a promising rising star in the ring, was left in a vegetative state with life-altering injuries. He was under the near-constant care of his family.

Colon's dad and former trainer, Richard, announced the heartbreaking news on social media, writing: 'Good morning, everyone. I regret to inform you of the passing of my son Prichard from this earthly world. He is now in a better place.'

He added: 'Thank you for so many years of love and prayers. As much as you can, please keep us in your prayers.'

Former boxer Prichard Colon has died at the age of 33, his family have announced

The Puerto Rican suffered catastrophic brain injuries during a 2015 fight (pictured)

Until that fateful fight almost 11 years ago, Colon had been one of the sport's most promising prospects.

He had established an unblemished 16-0 record with 13 knockouts with many in boxing viewing him as a future star.

Following the bout against Williams, Colon was rushed to the hospital where doctors discovered a subdural hematoma.

He underwent emergency surgery as medics desperately attempted to relieve the swelling in his brain. After spending 221 days in a coma, Colon awoke unable to walk or talk.

Despite the traumatic injuries, just three years ago, Colon had vowed not to throw in the towel.

In an update on his Facebook profile at the time, Colon attempted to speak with his mother and even raised a smile in a moving video.

The post was captioned: 'I will not give up'.

In other clips, the ex-fighter could be seen attending a truck rally with his family, while also appearing to take a positive step in being able to brush his own teeth.

He was left in a vegetative state and was under the near-constant care of his family

Until that fateful fight, Colon had been one of the sport's most promising prospects

His mother also shared a video of her son on his 31st birthday where she gave him a cupcake with a candle on it.

Colon's story is one of the most tragic in boxing history, with former heavyweight champion Deontay Wilder breaking down in tears while discussing it last year.

'We’ve seen what happens, look at Colon. How he got hit, Prichard Colon, correct,' Wilder said.

'This man didn’t have no kids… they don’t understand. Y’all don’t f****** understand what we go through, man.

'And I don’t even know him like that, but I will always be an advocate for us. Because this man will never know what it’s like to be somebody’s father. And that’s one of the most precious things in the world, to be somebody’s father. But he will never be nobody’s father, man.

'Because he got in the ring to support his family but now, his family got to take care of him for the rest of his life.'

Sports.title: Why Turkey has become the go-to destination this summer as Romelu Lukaku joins Mohamed Salah and Leandro Trossard in landing lucrative moves
Sports.content:
Romelu Lukaku became the latest big-name star to be greeted by a fanatical support after touching down in Turkey this week to complete a lucrative transfer.

Lukaku was decked out in Fenerbahce's black and yellow striped kit as he chanted towards the fans who had come out to celebrate the new arrival.

The 33-year-old will officially be unveiled at a welcoming ceremony on Friday at their stadium, with supporters again invited to come out in their numbers.

Lukaku is far from the first this summer to go through the welcoming process, following Leandro Trossard, Nathan Ake, Mason Greenwood, Dusan Vlahovic and most notably Mohamed Salah in joining clubs in the Turkish top flight.

He looks unlikely to be the last either with Galatasaray having tabled a £38million offer for Arsenal winger Gabriel Martinelli.

Daily Mail Sport, however, has reported that the 25-year-old Brazilian is not currently inclined to leave for Turkey.

Romelu Lukaku has signed for Fenerbahce, becoming the latest big name to move to the Turkish Super Lig

Mohamed Salah is the league's headline addition this summer following his departure from Liverpool

While Turkey has typically been a regular landing spot for well-known players – particularly those entering the final years of their careers, the comparison has been made this summer to the swathes of talent that moved to the Saudi Pro League in recent years.

Lucrative contracts have clearly been a factor, something that was highlighted by Salah's move to Trabzonspor.

'Under the terms of the agreement, the player will receive a total guaranteed payment of €17,000,000 (£14.5m) per football season, comprising an annual salary of €10,000,000 (£8.5m) and a signing fee of €7,000,000 (£6m),' Trabzonspor stated on a public disclosure platform.

'Additionally, the player will receive performance-based bonuses for each football season.

'Furthermore, under the image rights agreement, the player will receive a 20 per cent share of the revenue from products sold by our retail company that are specific to "Mohamed Salah."

'A payment amounting to five per cent of the gross remuneration payable to the player will be made as an agency fee.'

Salah is far from the only one, with former Juventus forward Vlahovic earning a guaranteed £6.4million-a-year over the next three seasons.

The finances are boosted further by Turkey's tax environment, with players receiving an exemption meaning they are due to pay a base 20 per cent rate, compared to normal progressive rates.

Clubs have typically worked to handle these tax implications, with the income tax accounted for as part of their payroll.

As such, the Telegraph reported that the announced figures will be the players' net pay, rather than gross pay that is subject to significant tax deductions.

Salah will earn £14.5m-a-year before bonuses after he signed for Trabzonspor

Dusan Vlahovic has also secured a lucrative contract, with players also benefiting from a favourable tax situation in Turkey

It is claimed this approach would lead to Salah taking home around £500,000-week, representing a sizeable increase on his wages while at Liverpool.

Daily Mail Sport reported last month that Turkish clubs have also made a concerted effort to ensure they can offer the best facilities and lifestyle to their new stars, ensuring they remain competitive with the likes of Saudi Arabia and MLS.

Galatasaray moved into a new 130-acre training facility last year which cost around £17.5m, alongside spending on upgrading their academy and other sports branches.

They have also invested in a private island in the middle of the Bosphorus Strait and turned it into an exclusive destination where players can enjoy parties and fine dining.

Besiktas moved into a fresh £86m stadium a decade ago and are planning to build a new training ground near Istanbul Airport.

They are currently saddled with debts of around £387m, as per their latest announcement, but hope to erase that via investment in a state-backed real estate project.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo unveils shock new look just days after marrying Georgina Rodriguez at intimate wedding ceremony
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo unveils shock new look just days after marrying Georgina Rodriguez at intimate wedding ceremony

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Cristiano Ronaldo has revealed an astonishing new hairstyle in the wake of his wedding to Georgina Rodriguez.

Gone is the black, slicked-back hair and in its place is a hairdo we never thought we'd see on him: a ginger buzz cut with a high skin fade.

The 41-year-old has been remarkably consistent with his look over the years but, with his fresh trim, it would now be hard to distinguish him from his old Manchester United team-mate Paul Scholes.

This could well be the haircut with which he passes his coveted 1,000 career goals mark.

The Al-Nassr star is on 976 goals for club and country and has a year left on his £488,000-a-day contract in Saudi Arabia.

Ronaldo was pictured returning to training, preparing for the season under new manager Ange Postecoglou alongside the likes of Sadio Mane and Kingsley Coman.

Cristiano Ronaldo debuted a bold new look as he returned to training with Al-Nassr

Just days ago he married Georgina Rodriguez in an 'intimate and private' ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, alongside their five children

CR7 finally broke his major trophy duck with Al-Nassr last campaign as they got their hands on the Saudi Pro League.

And on Tuesday he finally achieved his long-time dream of marrying Georgina in an 'intimate and private' ceremony with their five children present, a year after they first got engaged.

Ronaldo shared that he and Georgina had tied the knot after ten years together by sharing a snap of their wedding bands on Instagram.

A representative for Ronaldo also confirmed news of the union, saying: 'Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez were married today in a civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, and are now officially husband and wife.

'The ceremony was a private and intimate moment attended by their five children.'

Their wedding news came just days after it was thought the couple were set to marry in Funchal Cathedral, leading to thousands of fans gathering outside the church.

However, it was then revealed that the couple were not getting married there at all, and the ceremony turned out to be for an entirely unconnected Portuguese couple from Madeira called Fabio Ramos and Fatima Nicole Cunha Teixeira.

Georgina was working at a Gucci store in Madrid, earning £10 an hour, when she and Ronaldo met in 2016.

The Portugal star announced that he and Georgina had tied the knot by sharing a snap of their wedding bands on Instagram

The pair have two biological children, though she helps raise all five of his kids. Cristiano Jr. (pictured left) hugs his baby sister Eva while Georgina cradles Mateo on her lap, Cristiano (pictured right) holds his two daughters baby Bella and Alana Martina

Ronaldo, 41, is aiming to score 1,000 career goals and has a year left on his deal at Al-Nassr

Recalling their meeting, Georgina said: 'I was finally able to leave the shop to go home three hours later than I should have and as I was getting ready to leave Cristiano came in with his eldest son and some friends.

'Let's just say it was butterflies in my stomach.'

Cristiano would then pick Georgina up from work in his £1.5million Bugatti – after she had arrived at the shop on the bus.

'Many times he'd come after work', she said in her Netflix series I Am Georgina.

'He would come, I remember once, once in a Bugatti. My coworkers went crazy. They get there on the bus, and I would leave in a Bugatti. I mean people couldn't believe it.'

By December, she quit her job shortly after fans began crowding outside the store.

The following month, the pair made their first public appearance at The Best FIFA Football Awards, confirming speculation that they were a couple.

Cristiano and Georgina made their Instagram debut as a couple in March 2017 when the footballer posted a sweet snap of them cuddling on a couch.

Ronaldo proposed to Georgina last year with a huge diamond engagement, having previously said he 'waited' before popping the question

Georgina joked that the soccer star popping the question with an 'enormous' diamond ring was 'the least he could offer' after waiting for so long to propose

In June of that year, the footballer welcomed twins Mateo and Eva via surrogacy and then five months later, Georgina gave birth to their daughter, Alana Martina, in November.

The following month, Georgina posed for photos with her newborn daughter Alana for the cover of HOLA!

Revealing how they came up with the name for their daughter, she said: 'We both chose the name. Cristiano chose Alana and I chose Martina.

'We decided to give her both names that each of us chose. We thought it was even more special.'

In 2022, the couple welcomed twins; however, their baby boy tragically died during childbirth, while his sister, Bella Esmeralda, survived.

Opening up about how he and Georgina coped with the heartache of losing a baby, the footballer told Piers Morgan at the time: 'I feel that we always support each other. Sometimes it's like in a relationship you have good moments, bad moments it is part of the journey.

'But probably in that period, we consolidated it more, the relationship, but even in the worst moments you have to meet, you have to make the thing smooth.

'I learned so many things. I saw the other perspective of the life. My daughter, now who is three years old, she is the queen of the family, who made the house happy.

Cristiano met Georgina in 2016 after he saw her in the Gucci store where she was working

'Everything happens for a reason. I believe in that. So, we are a blessed family. I am proud of that.'

After nearly a decade together, fans were then desperate to know when Georgina and Cristiano would marry, with their family now complete.

However, in an interview with Marca last year, the Portuguese admitted he hadn't yet married Georgina because he hadn't felt the 'click'.

He said: 'I always tell her, "when we get that click". Like everything with our life, and she knows what I'm talking about.

'It could be in a year or it could be in six months or it could be in a month. I'm 1000 per cent sure that it'll happen.'

In August, the footballer finally popped the question with a giant diamond ring.

Fans speculated the pair got engaged the month before after the model shared pictures of a bridal-themed dinner, complete with 'C heart G' pillows, a six-piece band and stunning white flower arrangements.

She also wore a giant sparkler on her wedding ring finger, hinting at the pair's secret engagement.

Georgina gleefully shared the news on Instagram with a photo of her glitzy engagement ring. 'Yes I do. In this and in all my lives,' she wrote in a heartfelt caption.

Cristiano then revealed that two of his children inspired him to give Georgina a 'not-so romantic' and off-the-cuff proposal.

He revealed that he didn't plan to propose to the 'woman of his life' the night they got engaged, but it felt like the 'right time'.

'It was like 1am. My daughters were in bed sleeping,' the 41-year-old told Piers Morgan in part one of their new interview.

He said: 'One of my friends gave me the ring to offer Gio (Georgina) and as I was giving her the ring, my two kids come in and say "Daddy, you're going to give the ring to mum and you're going to ask her to get married."

'I said, "Wow, this is the right moment to say yes." It was the time. I knew that I was going to do it one day but I hadn't planned to do it then.

'Because my daughters said that and my friends were filming, it was what I wanted and I offered (the ring). I didn't (get on one knee) because I wasn't prepared but it was a beautiful moment. I made a speech.

'It was simple, I'm not a very romantic guy. Well, I am, but I'm not very romantic, not the kind of guy who brings flowers every week to the home. But I'm romantic in my way. It was beautiful and I knew that it's the woman of my life so I did that and I hope that I did it well.'

Asked about when they plan to tie the knot, the footballer joked: 'Not yet. We plan to do it after the World Cup with the trophy! But she is not the person that likes big parties. She doesn't like it. She likes private things. So I will respect these decisions.

'One thing that I love, she didn't care about the ring. She asked me if I was honest and I said, "I want you and I want to marry you." I didn't cry but I had tears on my eyes.'

Experts estimated that Cristiano splashed out an astonishing £1.5million on Georgina's engagement ring.

Sports.title: Chelsea still await bid for Enzo Fernandez despite looming deadline - as his suitors Man City agree to sell Tijjani Reijnders to Saudi Arabia: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Chelsea wait on Enzo bid and let Badiashile go

Chelsea have still to receive any bids for Enzo Fernandez - 23 hours ahead of their self-imposed deadline.

Manchester City are interested but have been told to submit a written £120m offer by 5pm on Friday.

Chelsea are among the clubs to have checked on Monaco's Lamine Camara.

The principality club rejected an offer from Crystal Palace for 22-year-old Camara earlier this week.

Chelsea have also agreed a deal with Napoli for defender Benoit Badiashile.

The Italian side will take the French centre-back on an initial loan for £2.6m with a further £800,000 in bonuses. There is an option to buy for £23m and Napoli will cover the 25-year-old's salary in full.

Chelsea are yet to receive a bid from Enzo Fernandez after setting a deadline of 5pm on Friday

Leeds stay on Elvedi trail

Leeds United are continuing to work on a deal for Borussia Monchengladbach centre-back Nico Elvedi.

The Switzerland international, who can also play at right-back, emerged as an option prior to the World Cup when Leeds discussed a £7m offer and has given the go-ahead for a move to Elland Road.

The 29-year-old worked under Leeds boss Daniel Farke previously when he was in charge of Monchengladbach.

Elvedi has two years to run on his contract though it's understood he could leave for £8.2m.

Bye-bye Reijnders

Tijjani Reijnders has agreed to join Al Qadsiah from Manchester City.

The Saudi Pro League club coached by former Celtic and Liverpool boss Brendan Rodgers agreed a £52million fee with City.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed, Nottingham Forest had made a proposal earlier this month for the 28-year-old Netherlands international and Galatasaray had made an approach in recent days.

Tijjani Reijnders missed City's open training after Al Qadsiah made an offer for him

Spence set for Italian job

Djed Spence will travel to Italy ahead of his Inter Milan medical tomorrow.

Tottenham have agreed to sell the England international for £26million and his former club Middlesbrough hold a percentage sell-on of the profit.

Spurs paid £20m to buy Spence from Boro in 2022.

City reject fresh Rodri bid

Manchester City and Barcelona continue to discuss a fee for midfielder Rodri.

City have dismissed Barca’s latest offer of around £55m as they hold out for closer to £68m for the Spain captain.

Meanwhile, City forward Jeremy Doku has signed a new contract at the Etihad that will keep him at the club until 2031, with an option for a further year.

The Belgium international said : ‘This club means so much to me – I have developed as both a player and a person. I feel settled here, and I know I am improving every day because of the work the staff here do.

‘It’s hard to explain just how much this Club does to help players. I don’t take it for granted and it makes me better.

‘With Enzo here now I am really excited about the new season. His style of football is the kind we love, so that’s exciting for the players.

‘The City fans are also a huge reason I have signed this new contract. I feel their love and support, and it means the world to me. I want to focus of bringing them the success they deserve.’

Barcelona have had a fresh £55million bid for Rodri rejected by Manchester City

Galatasaray move for Martinelli

Galatasaray have made their move for Arsenal winger Gabriel Martinelli with a £38million offer.

However, the Brazilian is not inclined to leave for Turkey.

The 25-year-old is one of the players Arsenal are prepared to listen to offers for with a valuation around £50m.

Roma have also shown interest and it is understood Martinelli will only consider options from the strongest leagues.

Arsenal are re-evaluating options to strengthen their left hand side, they are also continuing discussions with Aston Villa for centre back Ezri Konsa with their latest proposal understood to be around £40m for the centre back.

Besiktas in the frame for £18m Willock

Besiktas remain in the frame for Newcastle United midfielder Joe Willock.

The 26-year-old has one year left on contract and is valued around £18m. Premier League sides have also shown interest while Besiktas had an offer rejected early this month.

Race for Nwaneri heats up

Interest is building in Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri who is considering his options and whether to depart this window.

A number of clubs, including RB Leipzig and other Premier League sides, have been looking to take the 19-year-old on loan or potentially a permanent basis after his disappointing spell with Marseille last season.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta praised the England U21 international after his return to pre-season training, saying: ‘Ethan has been really good, probably what happened on the field on his loan in Marseille wasn’t what was expected, and there was a lot of noise and change around the club.

‘But he looks different, a lot more mature, it’s incredible what six months and a different experience abroad can do to you - to be abroad on your own, to go through tough times and to witness that is a part of football you have to be good enough to cope with. I’m very happy with what Ethan has done in pre-season.’

Nwaneri joined Arsenal's academy aged eight and made his Premier League debut against Brentford in September 2022, becoming the youngest player to appear in the English top flight, at 15 years and 181 days old.

He has made 34 appearances for Arsenal and though only made nine appearances at Marseille, still managed to score two goals.

Pape Sarr a target for Al Ahli

Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr is emerging as a target for Al Ahli in the Saudi Pro League.

The 23-year-old will be allowed to leave if suitable offers arrive and has been the subject of interest from Brentford and Aston Villa as well as other European sides.

Spurs beat off strong competition to sign Sarr from Metz in 2021 and, while he has shown glimpses of what he is capable of, the Senegal international has been inconsistent overall, as have the majority of the squad in recent seasons.

The arrival of Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali mean his starting opportunities will be limited and he is open to exploring a move away.

Spurs are looking to wrap up the sales of Cristian Romero to Atletico and Djed Spence to Inter today.

They remain keen on Manchester City’s Savinho and Cody Gakpo of Liverpool. City’s Omar Marmoush is also on their list.

Villa expected to reject Arsenal offer for Konsa

Aston Villa were expected to turn down Arsenal’s initial proposal of £40million for Ezri Konsa, who is thought to be open to the move.

Villa are also looking to close deals for midfielder Joao Palhinha and left-back Matteo Ruggeri.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Ezri Konsa is said to be open to a move to the Premier League champions Arsenal

United youngster Williams joins Peterborough

Manchester United winger Ethan Williams has joined Peterborough United for a ‘sizeable’ undisclosed fee.

The 20-year-old, who was part of United’s pre-season tour of Finland, Norway and Sweden, has signed a long-term deal.

Williams had spent time on loan at League Two Cheltenham Town and Scottish Premiership outfit Falkirk.

He said: ‘I have enjoyed my time at [Manchester] United and it's always tough to leave a place like that, but there comes a time in your career where you have to make tough decisions to develop yourself and Peterborough is renowned for helping younger players.’

United’s deal also includes add-ons, a 50percent sell-on clause, a buy-back option and matching rights.

Tigers making moves in the market

Leeds United forward Joe Gelhardt has completed his medical at Hull City ahead of his £4.5million move.

He has agreed a four year contract with option for a further year. Wrexham and Rangers had also made efforts to sign the 24-year-old.

Meanwhile, Hull have formalised their interest in Everton midfielder Tim Iroegbunam with an offer understood to be in excess of £15million.

The 23-year-old has a year left on contract.

If it ain't So?

Brazilian side Palmeiras have signed Fabio So from Burnley.

The 18-year-old made 15 appearances in the U18 Premier League for Burnley, as well as a couple of appearances for the U21s. He left on a free transfer and has signed a contract until the end of January. The contract includes the possibility of an automatic renewal.

Portuguese midfielder So joined Burnley after being at Newcastle's academy.

Amorim's Milan exodus

AC Milan coach Ruben Amorim has decided Fikayo Tomori and Christopher Nkunku do not figure in his plans this season.

The former Chelsea players are available for sale along with midfielder Youssouf Fofana.

David Odogu, Pervis Estupinan, Santiago Gimenez and Philip Terracciano are also expected to leave.

Fikayo Tomori is one of eight AC Milan players who have been put up for sale by Ruben Amorim

Ge-Evan-noa

Brighton striker Evan Ferguson is a target for Genoa.

The Republic of Ireland international was on loan in Serie A at Roma last season, where he scored five goals in 22 appearances, and rivals Genoa would like him to return.

The 21-year-old has been hindered by niggling injuries and damaged his ankle in March but he is also attracting Premier League interest.

Reds youngsters on the move

Liverpool left-back Calum Scanlon is closing on a loan to Cardiff City.

The 21-year-old spent the second half of last season on loan at Cardiff and they have been working hard to bring him back.

Scanlon has impressed on Liverpool's pre-season and attracted a number of enquiries.

League One Sheffield Wednesday, notably, made concerted effort to take the England U20 international to Hillsborough.

Liverpool midfielder James McConnell is a loan target for Championship side Preston North End.

A number of other Championship teams have enquired for the 21-year-old plus League One Leicester City.

Meanwhile, Arsenal are closing in agreement for 16-year-old striker Vincent Joseph who had decided to leave Liverpool last month.

Liverpool offered the teenager a scholarship but he declined and talks are ongoing over compensation.

The last teenager to leave Liverpool for another Premier League club was Isaac Moran. He left for Newcastle United earlier this year and a subsequent tribunal resulted in a seven-figure fee being payable to Liverpool with the settlement having the potential to reach £5m.

TUESDAY: Roy Keane's son-in-law linked with move to Portugal

MONDAY: West Ham interested in free agent Jamie Vardy

SUNDAY: Everton and Crystal Palace in advanced talks over McNeil-Johnson swap

SATURDAY: West Ham and Tottenham agree £5m fee for Manor Solomon

FRIDAY: Rodri tells Real Madrid he wishes to join Barcelona

THURSDAY: Man City target new goalkeeper after James Trafford sale

Sports.title: Revealed: What Diego Simeone told Julian Alvarez in showdown talks after Arsenal target reiterated his desire to leave Atletico Madrid
Sports.content:
Revealed: What Diego Simeone told Julian Alvarez in showdown talks after Arsenal target reiterated his desire to leave Atletico Madrid

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Julian Alvarez has spoken to Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone for the first time since declaring that he wants to leave the club in order to 'fulfil my dream'.

The highly coveted Argentina forward, 26, is being tracked by several of Europe's biggest clubs, including Premier League champions Arsenal, LaLiga champions Barcelona and Real Madrid.

While representing Argentina at this summer's World Cup, Alvarez publicly declared his desire to leave Atletico, saying: 'I try to be an honest person. I spoke with the people at Atletico Madrid, and I think the best thing for everyone is a transfer. I want to fulfill my dream.'

Although reports have suggested Barcelona are Alvarez's preferred destination, Atletico have remained steadfast in their position that he is not for sale. Chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin said last month that the club would not entertain any offers for the striker, even in the region of £170m (€200 million).

Alvarez has a £428m (€500m) release clause and Atletico have already rejected a £129m (€150m) bid from Real Madrid.

The striker returned to pre-season training this week and, ahead of Wednesday's session, reportedly spent around 10 minutes speaking with Simeone at Atletico's Cerro del Espino training complex.

The striker returned to pre-season training this week after publicly declaring he would like to leave the club this summer in order to 'fulfil my dream'

Alvarez reportedly spent around 10 minutes speaking with Simeone (above) at Atletico's Cerro del Espino training complex, and reiterated his desire to leave during the conversation

According to reports, Alvarez, who is nicknamed La Arana, or 'The Spider', because of his Spider-Man celebration, reiterated his desire to leave during the conversation.

In response, Simeone is said to have restated the position he outlined publicly last week, namely that Atletico are planning for Alvarez to remain at the club.

'The situation is very clear, the club made a decision that Miguel Angel explained very well,' Simeone said. 'We are very happy with Julian. From a sporting perspective, we will help him to continue growing, to continue improving, and to give us back what he has given us in these two years, which was a great deal.'

The former Manchester City player, who won the 2022 World Cup with Argentina, joined Atletico in an £81.5m deal in 2024. He recorded 20 goals and nine assists in all competitions last season, while his 10 Champions League goals left him behind only Mbappe and Harry Kane in the scoring charts.

Back in April, Simeone said: 'I am not in Julian Alvarez's head. I suppose it is normal that an extraordinary player like Julian is wanted by Arsenal, Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona. It's normal because he's very good.'

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, meanwhile, has admitted there are 'very few players' in world football capable of immediately improving his starting XI, but insists the Gunners are still trying to make another marquee signing this summer.

Arsenal were heavily linked with Vinicius Jr before he signed a new contract with Real Madrid. They have, however, already secured the signing of Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes for £75m.

The former Manchester City player, who won the 2022 World Cup with Argentina, joined Atletico in an £81.5m deal in 2024

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, meanwhile, has insisted that the Gunners are still trying to make another marquee signing this summer

'I think for the margins to improve, there are very few players in the market that are available to do that and bring that to the club,' Arteta said after Arsenal's 1-1 draw with Como on Wednesday.

'Every time we have an opportunity to improve the squad and bring more quality and depth to the squad, we need to do that,' he said. 'We are actively trying to do so. The thing in the market is that it doesn't just depend on you. We are very clear on that.'

With more than two weeks remaining in the transfer window, there is still plenty of time for the situation to develop, while Arsenal may also benefit from Atletico's strained relationship with their LaLiga rivals.

One example came in June after Atletico rejected Real Madrid's £129m offer for Alvarez.

Real released a statement saying: 'Following the meeting of the board of directors held today, it has made an offer of 150 million euros to Club Atletico de Madrid for the federative rights of the player Julian Alvarez.

'After reviewing and evaluating the offer, Club Atletico de Madrid has expressed its gratitude for the proposal, made within the framework of the good relations between both clubs, and has rejected it, referring to the player's release clause.'

Atletico quoted the statement on X alongside a series of laughing emojis.

In a follow-up post, they added: 'You must have confused education with gratitude, but to leave no doubt: we don't thank you for anything.

'We neither study nor consider any offer for Julian. How could we not get along, when you make us laugh even more than Barcelona does.'

In a final swipe, Atletico posted: 'P.S. Taking advantage of the good relationship with your new president, let's see if you stop 'stealing' players from our Academy. Thanks a lot, @realmadrid!'

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
